sed -n 182,186p model/model.py; sed -n 238,246p model/model.py; sed -n 70,108p model/train.py; sed -n 640,648p model/train.py

result:
Experiment 28 is implemented: the in-graph resize in `model/model.py` now enlarges the 128 px frame to 288 px instead of 224 px. Both modules import cleanly. The trunk loads strictly from `effb0_features7.pt` and passed its built-in shape check at 288 px. I did not run training; the harness does that.

**The change:** `INPUT_PX` went from 224 to 288. The two feature levels the model reads come out 18×18 and 9×9 instead of 14×14 and 7×7. The parameter count is unchanged, so the exported ONNX should stay about 31.7 MB, under the 32 MiB limit. The external input is still 1×3×128×128, and decode, confidence, losses, augmentation, batch size 64, MixStyle, SWA and learning rates are untouched.

**Docs and comments:**
- `model/model.py`: added a docstring section, "LARGER IN-GRAPH ENLARGEMENT (… experiment 28)", and updated every comment that described the old 224 px shapes.
- `model/train.py`: added an "experiment 28: 224 → 288" note and fixed the size comments.

**One deviation from "no logic change" in `train.py`:** one description string in `train_info.json` had "14x14"/"7x7" written in by hand. I made it read the sizes from `MID_HW`/`DEEP_HW` so the record says 18×18 / 9×9. It changes only that text.

The pretrained weights still load from the file in `model/pretrained/`, as the brief requires. The standing rule says not to rely on a local weight file, because the remote trainer receives only `model.py` and `train.py`. The current champion already loads its weights this way, so I left it as it was. If the remote run can't find that file, this is the cause.
